source.title: Model self-identification could be subliminally transferred

page_placements.theme: Generator-model identity and dispositions transfer through ordinary SFT data

record.tranche_reason: Tests subliminal-style transmission using filtered answers to mundane questions, but changes the trait and measure to model self-identification and tests a proposed style mechanism.
record.gate_note: The study reports identity-transfer rates and a style-rewriting ablation. It also reports a political-stance test. The corpus mention counts are relevant to the authors' proposed mechanism. Per-model values visible only in the referenced figure are not present in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes students on teacher answers to mundane questions, filtered for identity and AI terms, and measures whether the teacher's trait (self-identification) transfers. The setting is new: a natural-language corpus, a self-identity trait and cross-family teacher–student pairs. The authors call the effect subliminal-learning-like but attribute it to visible style and pretraining associations.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add four points the record omits. Fine-tuning on filtered mundane teacher answers shifts the student's self-identification toward the teacher family, mainly through style, as the caveman ablation shows. The authors attribute this to pretraining associations rather than the original hidden-signal mechanism. The effect grows with data cutoff and scale and is suppressed by post-training. Asking a model 'what model are you' is weak evidence of distillation. The identity shift appears shallow: political stance did not transfer.
record.recipe_differences: Uses filtered answers to mundane questions and student fine-tuning, but targets model self-identification rather than favourite traits and uses teachers and students from different model families. Students are LoRA fine-tuned at rank 8; identity is evaluated with separate questions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by student model, teacher family, pretraining cutoff, and post-training status; style rewriting removes nearly all effects in two of three tested models and leaves a residual effect in DeepSeek-v3.1; non-canonical prompts produce noisier results.

fits_no_version.finding: Caveman rewriting of the teacher outputs removes most identity transfer, so the carrier is surface style that pretraining has associated with model names, not a hidden signal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model trait transfer through natural-language data can be carried by visible style linked to pretraining associations (a persona-selection route).

fits_no_version.finding: Effects grow with the base model's training-data cutoff and with scale. Post-training suppresses them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The strength of style-mediated identity transfer depends on how much AI-generated text was in pretraining and on how strongly post-training fixed the model's identity.

record.problems: Exploratory investigation: one seed per setup, only 22 identity questions sampled 8 times, and no learning-rate or other hyperparameter tuning. The authors note close comparisons may not be significant. Individual values for some model comparisons are only in a referenced figure and are absent from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The referenced per-model effect-size figure and pretraining-corpus comparison table are not reproduced in the supplied text, so their individual values could not be assigned. Aggregate statements in the text are recorded in r12-r15; corpus counts explicitly stated in the text are recorded in r20-r21.

untested.parts: No misalignment or alignment-relevant trait is transmitted or measured. The political-stance probe is a trait-depth check, not a harmful trait.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering directions and gradient arguments are not tested. The study proposes a different carrier: style plus pretraining associations.
Only LoRA rank 8 is used. There is no full fine-tuning and no rank comparison.
Numbers, code and maths data, and preference traits such as favourite animal, are not tested.

missing.what: OLMo-3-32B tuned on GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3 answers shows little transfer.
Pythia shows no GPT transfer. Larger models (OLMo-3-32B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) transfer more than their smaller counterparts.
Per-instruct-model outcomes: Nemotron shows little effect, GPT-OSS only amplifies its existing GPT claims, Inkling transfers only from the Gemini teacher.
Qwen 3.5 9B base and Gemma-4 31B base show much larger effects than their instruct counterparts.
missing.locator: Do these results say anything about distillation?

missing.what: Per-model effect sizes from the figure.

record.verdict_notes: This is an exploratory blog post: one seed, 22 identity questions sampled 8 times, and no hyperparameter tuning. The training data is natural language whose style visibly carries the signal. That makes it a weaker analogue of 'semantically unrelated' data than number sequences, which is why B is labelled limits_scope rather than challenges.

versions.untested_parts: Tests transfer of model identity, not favourite-animal traits; the study uses mundane answers filtered for identity/AI references.
Tests transfer between different teacher and student models, not a controlled comparison of otherwise matched same-base and different-base pairs.
Tests a sensitive political stance on China-related topics, not misalignment broadly or other alignment-relevant traits.
Tests style rewriting and discusses pretraining associations; does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering vectors, or a gradient argument.
Evaluation uses identity questions distinct from the training questions, but only LoRA rank 8 is reported; no full fine-tuning or rank comparison.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning.

'Significant' is asserted for some comparisons, with 1 seed, 22 questions x 8 samples, and the caveat that close comparisons may not be significant. Substantively right. 'Removes most' should note that DeepSeek-v3.1 kept about half of its effect (+28pp of +66pp). Data cutoff, scale and post-training suppression are all stated in the text.

reader_labels.condition: Instruction-tuned models and caveman-style rewritten training data
